assessment.rationale: No AI system has made a Nobel-worthy discovery without human guidance, so the Main KPI of 1 autonomous Nobel-worthy discovery is unmet. The strongest open systems reach workshop level: Sakana's open-source AI Scientist-v2 submitted three fully autonomous manuscripts to an ICLR workshop and one exceeded the average human acceptance threshold (https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2504.08066). Kosmos runs up to 12 hours on a human-supplied objective and dataset; independent scientists judged 79.4% of its statements accurate, and of seven highlighted findings three reproduced unpublished results and four were new (https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2511.02824). Google's Co-Scientist (Nature 2026, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10644-y) works with human scientists. A 2026 critique argues agentic AI scientists are not built for autonomous discovery (https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2605.08956). Open code is plentiful (SakanaAI/AI-Scientist about 14,950 stars, AI-Scientist-v2 about 7,446). Class neutral: large potential benefit, but autonomous discovery systems raise dual-use and verification risks. Honest limit: running the open AI Scientist or Kosmos-style loops is a known baseline and not new work, and Nobel-worthiness cannot be attested quickly by checkers; tasks must be bounded, checkable steps such as an autonomous result independently replicated and judged new by domain experts.

additionalSearches.query: AI Scientist fully automated open-ended scientific discovery (2024 onward)
additionalSearches.finding: 13,656 works: The AI Scientist (2024, 430 citations), AI Scientist-v2 workshop-level discovery (2025), Kosmos (2025), Co-Scientist and a multi-agent discovery system in Nature (2026). Workshop-level and human-collaborative results, nothing Nobel-level.
3,589 repositories: SakanaAI/AI-Scientist (14,950 stars), AI-Scientist-v2 (7,446), EvoScientist, openscience workbench. Open agents exist; none credited with a major autonomous discovery.

additionalSearches.query: autonomous AI discovery novel scientific finding validated without human (2024 onward)
additionalSearches.finding: 19,407 works: Kosmos, surveys of agentic science, and the 2026 critique 'Agentic AI Scientists Are Not Built For Autonomous Scientific Discovery'. No validated landmark autonomous discovery.

additionalSearches.query: robot scientist Adam Eve autonomous hypothesis (2024 onward)
additionalSearches.finding: 242 works: histories of AI scientists, a survey on the verification gap of autonomous research agents (2026), and how far AI scientists are from changing the world (EMNLP 2026). Verification is the named gap.

additionalSearches.query: Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery
additionalSearches.finding: Up to 12-hour runs, about 42,000 lines of code and 1,500 papers per run; 79.4% of statements judged accurate; seven discoveries, three reproducing unpublished results and four new; humans supply objective and dataset.
End-to-end agentic tree search; three fully autonomous manuscripts submitted to an ICLR workshop, one exceeding the average human acceptance threshold.
